**(B)** one

At fertilization the coverings of the male and female pronuclei degenerate and the two fuse (syngamy or karyogamy) into a single diploid synkaryon, so the zygote has one nucleus. Two nuclei are present only briefly as separate pronuclei, before the zygote is formed.

**(C)** testes

The testes are the primary male sex organs (gonads) that produce sperms and testosterone. Sperm is the male gamete and seminal fluid is a secretion of the accessory glands, so neither is an organ, while the ovary is the female gonad.

**(D)** implantation

Implantation is the embedding of the blastocyst into the endometrium of the uterus, usually in the fundus. Fertilization is fusion of gametes in the ampulla, cleavage is the early mitotic division of the zygote, and gestation is the whole period of pregnancy.

**(C)** ovulation

Ovulation is the rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and release of the ovum (secondary oocyte), usually on the 14th day of the cycle under an LH surge. Capacitation is the activation of sperms in the female tract, gestation is pregnancy, and copulation is the act of mating.

**(A)** After about7 days of fertilization

The blastocyst floats in the uterine cavity until about the end of the 7th day, and implantation usually begins on day 7 after fertilization and is complete by the end of the 10th day. By three weeks the embryo is already embedded and gastrulation is under way.

**(C)** In vitro fertilization

In a test tube baby the egg is fertilized by sperm outside the body, in a test tube or glass plate, and the early embryo is then transferred to the mother, which is in vitro fertilization. Artificial insemination introduces sperms into the female tract so that fertilization happens in vivo, inside the body.

**(D)** A

In the figure the label A points to the cap at the very tip of the sperm head. The acrosome is the cap-like structure above the nucleus, formed from the Golgi body, and carries the lytic enzymes used to penetrate the egg. The labels below it mark the nucleus of the head and the neck and middle piece regions.

**(B)** secondary sexual character

Beard, moustache, chest hair, a muscular body and an enlarged larynx are external features that distinguish males from females, appearing at puberty under testosterone; the chapter calls these secondary sexual characters. A beard is not an organ at all, and the primary sex organs are the gonads.
